udt_struct_v0.doc: An Aqua chained swap. `hops` are `(sorted_token_pair, pool_index, token_out)`\nexactly as `swap_chained` expects; the bot builds them from its quotes.
udt_struct_v0.name: AquaSwap

udt_struct_v0.doc: A Soroswap multi-hop swap. `amount_in == 0` means "everything we hold of\n`path[0]`", which is how a second step consumes the first step's output\nwithout the planner having to predict it exactly.
udt_struct_v0.name: SoroswapSwap

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A plan armed on a receiver, waiting for the pool's `exec_op` callback.

`initiator` is the `from` of the flash loan -- the address Blend will pass as
`caller` and the address the receiver hands the funds back to. Recorded at
arming time by the receiver's owner, because Soroban gives a callee no way to
learn who invoked it.

Lives in *temporary* storage for the duration of one transaction: written by
`set_plan`, consumed by `exec_op`. Soroban executes a transaction
sequentially, so nothing can observe or race it in between.
udt_struct_v0.name: Plan

function_v0.doc:
Pull a balance off a receiver this contract owns, back here. Owner only.

A receiver's owner is a contract, and a contract cannot sign, so
without this any token that ever landed on a receiver -- a mistaken
transfer, a plan cut short -- would have no way out. This contract is
the receiver's owner and its direct invoker here, so the receiver's
owner check is met by invoker authorization; `withdraw` then sweeps it
the rest of the way to the account.
function_v0.name: sweep

udt_struct_v0.doc: Mirror of Blend's `Request`, declared here so it appears in this contract's\nown spec. The SDK's type is `export = false`, which leaves clients unable to\nencode arguments for `flash_execute`. Same fields, same wire encoding.
udt_struct_v0.name: Request

function_v0.doc:
Blend's flash-loan callback (`moderc3156::FlashLoan`). Called by the pool
after it has transferred the loan here and before it settles requests.

Runs the armed plan, then hands *everything* we hold of `token` back to
`caller`, whose `Repay` request the pool collects next. Anything above the
loan is profit and lands with the initiator too.
function_v0.name: exec_op

function_v0.doc:
Run a plan against funds this contract already holds. Owner only.

Cross-venue arbitrage without a flash loan, and the unwind path for a
liquidation position.
function_v0.name: execute

function_v0.doc:
Replace this contract's code in place. Owner only.

Storage -- the owner and any held balances -- survives, so a fix ships
without redeploying, re-funding and re-pointing the bot.
function_v0.name: upgrade

function_v0.doc:
Arm the plan that the next `exec_op` will run, and record who the loan's
`from` will be. Owner only, single-use.

Callable by an initiator contract (owner == initiator, in one
transaction) or by a wallet that owns this receiver directly and starts
the flash loan itself in a following transaction -- Blend's canonical
pattern, at the cost of a second ledger.
function_v0.name: set_plan

udt_struct_v0.doc: XOXNO Lending's market key: a listed asset on one of its hubs. Mirrors\n`common::types::HubAssetKey` in github.com/XOXNO/rs-lending-xlm field for\nfield, which is its wire encoding.
udt_struct_v0.name: HubAssetKey

udt_struct_v0.doc: A token and an amount: one repay or withdraw leg of an auction fill.
udt_struct_v0.name: TokenAmount

function_v0.doc:
`execute`, for a looped plan: the first `hard` steps must succeed, and
each later step runs only while it pays (`venues::run_steps_soft`). A
later pass that would lose ends the plan there with the earlier passes
kept, instead of reverting all of them. Owner only. Returns the output
of every step that ran.
function_v0.name: execute_soft

function_v0.doc:
Fill `percent` of `user`'s liquidation auction on `pool` from funds this
contract holds, and come out flat in the same transaction. Owner only.

One `submit` does the whole Blend side: the fill puts the auction's
lot (collateral) and bid (debt) on our position; the `repay` legs
clear the debt from what we hold (Blend caps repayment at the debt,
so over-asking is safe); the `withdraw` legs pull the collateral out
(Blend caps a withdrawal at the position, so over-asking is safe
there too). Then `steps` sell the collateral for `profit_token`.

Two guards make it safe to send on a quote: the position must end
with no debt and no collateral, and our `profit_token` balance must
have grown by at least `min_profit`. Either failing reverts the lot.
Returns the gain in `profit_token`.
function_v0.name: fill_auction

function_v0.doc: `owner` is the only address that can arm a plan, start a flash loan, run\na plan from held funds, or withdraw.
function_v0.name: __constructor

function_v0.doc:
Borrow `amount` of `asset` from `pool`, have `receiver` run `steps` with
it, then let the pool settle `requests` against us. Owner only.

For a pure arbitrage, `requests` is a single `Repay` of `amount` plus a
hair (dToken rounding at non-unit rates; Blend caps repayment at the
outstanding debt, so over-asking is safe). For a liquidation it is the
auction fill plus repayment of the liquidated debt, and we exit holding a
healthy position to unwind later.

Returns the change in our `asset` balance: realised profit.
function_v0.name: flash_execute

function_v0.doc: Replace a receiver's code. Owner only. The receiver's owner is this\ncontract, which cannot sign, so this is the only way its code moves.
function_v0.name: upgrade_receiver

function_v0.doc:
XOXNO's flash-loan callback. Called by its pool after it has sent the
loan here; on return the pool pulls `amount + fee` back with
`transfer_from` and reverts everything if it cannot.

Runs the armed plan with whatever this receiver holds (the loan, plus
any capital the initiator sent along), approves the pool for exactly
the repayment, and hands the rest to the initiator. Like `exec_op` it
does nothing unless the owner armed a plan in this same transaction
and `initiator` is the address that plan names.
function_v0.name: execute_flash_loan

function_v0.doc:
Borrow `amount` of `asset` from XOXNO Lending (`controller`, market
`hub_id`), have `receiver` run `steps` with the loan plus `own_amount`
of our own balance, and keep what is left after the loan and its fee
are repaid. Owner only. Returns the change in our balance of `asset`,
and reverts everything unless that is at least `min_profit`: the steps'
own guards say what each swap must return, this says what the whole
transaction must leave us with, fee included.
function_v0.name: flash_execute_xoxno
